## Why

Two chat sessions showed the coordinator using waypoints in ways that are hard to trace or that the user didn't want. A waypoint is a place a day's drive passes through without stopping, to steer the route (the coordinator's itinerary terms, technical spec 5.2).

1. **Empty `set_waypoints` calls that do nothing.** The coordinator's instructions say: "When the user approves fastest on a day, also clear the day's waypoints with set_waypoints and an empty list, in the same turn." The coordinator follows this even when the day has no waypoints, so the call changes nothing. Both cases below were like that. Code already removes a day's waypoints when the day is marked a rest day (domain model 4.5). If approving fastest did the same, the coordinator couldn't forget the step, and wouldn't make calls that do nothing.
2. **A waypoint picked as a sight, not as a point on the road.** With `routePreference: scenic`, the coordinator wanted San Francisco Day 1 on I-280 rather than US-101. It picked the Pulgas Water Temple as the waypoint. The temple sits off I-280 on Cañada Road, so the route left the freeway to pass through it: road time went from 2 h 29 m to 2 h 48 m. Then the reply told the user "We take I-280 past the Pulgas Water Temple, a quirky little spot," so it read as a stop the user hadn't asked for. The user had it taken off (#163). The domain model already says a waypoint sits on the road the coordinator wants (3.6 and 4.7). The coordinator's instructions don't say so, and don't say a waypoint isn't a stop. By contrast, in a later session it picked Belfast and Wiscasset, towns US-1 runs through, which added 3 minutes and 0 minutes.
3. **A waypoint holds no reason.** Waypoints are set for different reasons: to steer onto a scenic road, to make sure the route reaches a must-see area or road, or because the user asked for a road. Nothing on the waypoint says which. So when waypoints are cleared, the coordinator can't tell which ones it still needs without matching them against the trip brief's must-sees, and in a later session it has no memory of setting them. Someone reading the itinerary can't tell either: the Pulgas Water Temple waypoint would have shown "steer onto I-280", which makes the bad pick plain without reading the trace. Approvals and tier rules already carry their reasons this way.

## Where to look

Traces in Phoenix (DEVELOPMENT.md section 2):

- Live site, project `road-trip-agent`, session `12e986d6-2433-4e8d-b6ba-7ed2e4625c7b`. The empty call is span `6cdca9c8fb609fa8` (tool call `toolu_01SocX9RYr5ad1RoQG4qa7sB`), on Day 1, right after `update_day` approved fastest. The Belfast and Wiscasset waypoints are in the same turn.
- Local, project `road-trip-agent-local`, session `0458e3f3-2dc2-41ce-8f19-1c6ca0fa11f4`. The empty call is span `dd56be8d3fc8447d`, on Day 3, right after `update_day` approved fastest. The Pulgas Water Temple waypoint is set in the first turn, after the coordinator's reasoning "I'm considering I-280 as the scenic freeway option from SF toward Mountain View."

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 4.2 (must-sees that aren't one place, and the route preference), section 5.2 (the itinerary terms, and the rule for approving fastest), and section 8 (route type).
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 3.6 (Day: waypoints), 4.5 (`DaysService.approveRouteType()`), and 4.7 (how a leg is routed).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1 (`update_day`, `set_waypoints`, and `read_itinerary`).
- [Persistence](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), section 1 (migrations).

## Open questions

- ~~Clearing waypoints in code when fastest is approved also clears one set for a must-see area or road on that day. What does the coordinator do about those?~~ Settled 2026-10-27 in chat with Joe: each waypoint carries a reason, and `update_day`'s reply names each waypoint it cleared, with its reason. After approving fastest, the coordinator puts back, with `set_waypoints`, each cleared waypoint whose reason is a must-see or a user's request, and drops the ones that only steered toward the scenic road. It tells the user in one line what it dropped. See Do.

## Do

- **Each waypoint carries a reason.** `set_waypoints` takes each waypoint as a place ID and a reason, both required, such as "steer onto US-1", "must-see: Capitol Reef", or "the user asked: the Golden Gate Bridge". The day stores the reason with the place. `read_itinerary`'s leg line and `set_waypoints`' reply show each waypoint with its reason. The leg's `routedWaypoints` stays places only, since it records what Google was asked. Add a migration that gives waypoints in saved trips a reason that says none was recorded. Change domain model 3.6 (Day: waypoints, and its sentence "Users don't pick waypoints", since a user can ask for a road), tool design 2.1, and the coordinator's itinerary section in technical spec 5.2 to match. The downloads in `src/api/plan-downloads.ts` show the stored shape, so check they still read well.
- **Approving fastest clears the day's waypoints in code.** In `DaysService.approveRouteType()`, approving fastest clears the day's waypoints. Approving scenic leaves them alone. The leg is re-routed at the end of the write, as usual. `update_day`'s reply names each waypoint it cleared, with its reason, and gives the leg's new road time. Say so in `update_day`'s description, and change domain model 4.5, tool design 2.1, and technical spec section 8 to match. Replace the instruction to clear them with `set_waypoints` in the coordinator's instructions and technical spec 5.2 with the rule from the settled open question. Add tests with fakes (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5).
- **Say how to pick a waypoint.** In the coordinator's instructions (the itinerary terms or the waypoint rules), and in technical spec 4.2 and 5.2, say:
  - A waypoint is a place on the road itself, such as a town or a junction the road runs through, not a sight beside it.
  - A waypoint isn't a stop. A place worth seeing becomes a stop the user agrees to. Don't describe a waypoint to the user as a sight.
  - Check the road time in `set_waypoints`' reply. A waypoint that adds much more than a few minutes is a detour: pick another point on the road. One that adds nothing isn't needed, since the route already takes that road.
- The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.

## Done when

- `set_waypoints` refuses a waypoint without a reason, and `read_itinerary` shows each waypoint's reason. Tests show both.
- Approving fastest on a day with waypoints clears them, and the reply names each one with its reason and gives the leg's new road time. A test shows it.
- The migration runs locally on a trip with waypoints, and the trip still loads.
- The coordinator's view file has no instruction to clear waypoints with an empty list, and has the rule for putting waypoints back and the waypoint guidance above.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.
